author: Kevin Carter
title: Insights Into The Online World
text:
The adoption of the internet has been both evolutionary and revolutionary. It has changed the way we live, communicate and do business. The growth in the number of internet users and uses have been phenomenal. In many areas, such as the U.S., growth is beginning to level off as penetration rates hit high levels. In other areas, such as the emerging markets, that growth is just beginning.
Mary Meeker was one of the best known internet analysts during the 1990’s and 2000’s. At Morgan Stanley, she served as analyst when the firm brought Netscape and Google public. She has published many books and articles on new technologies. Currently, she is working as a venture capitalist. She publishes a comprehensive review of internet trends .* Her review is both informative and insightful.
Key takeaways from her most recent review show that internet usage continues to grow at a healthy pace. The shift to mobile continues as devices and application become better, faster, and easier to use. While data privacy has become a big concern, increased access to data helps companies create more personalized experiences for users.
Investors can capitalize on these trends by investing in internet companies such as Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) and Amazon (Amazon), smartphone manufacturers such as Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), subscriber services such as Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX ). In the emerging markets where adoption is particularly strong, investors can invest in market leaders like Alibaba (NYSE: BABA ), Baidu (NASDAQ: BIDU ) and Tencent ( OTCPK:TCEHY ) Or they can purchase funds that invest in these companies. The Emerging Markets Internet and Ecommerce ETF (NYSEARCA: EMQQ ) – can potentially provide investor’s exposure as these trends unfold in the emerging markets.
User Growth Plateauing The number of global internet users has reached 3.6 billion and represents roughly half the globe’s population. While the number of internet users continues to grow, it is growing a slower rate; 7% growth in 2017 vs. 12% in 2016. Growth in new smartphone shipments was 0% highlighting the already high rate of penetration. Remember, trees don’t grow to the skies.
But Overall Usage Continue to Grow However, growth in internet usage remains strong. Globally, daily hours spend on digital media per adult grew 4% during 2017 to 5.9 hours. Smartphone devices have become better, faster, and cheaper. Applications have become easier to use, prompting increased use of smartphones. The use of mobile payments is rising rapidly, particularly in China where the number of users has eclipsed 500 million. Mobile video viewing is also rapidly increasing, reaching near 30 minutes per viewer in 2017 as new formats continue to emerge.
Data – A Concern and a Benefit While data continues to be of prime concern, and for good reason, it also allows internet sites to improve the overall online experience for consumers and provide a more tailored offering. The Google Machine learning word accuracy rate approached 95%, that of a human. This has allowed services such as Amazon Echo, Spotify, Netflix and many others to improve the experience for users.
Continued Investment Investment in the technology space shows strength. Investment in technology companies, either through public or private financing over the past four years is at its highest level since the dot.com era. Growth in research & development was strongest among technology companies. R&D spending accelerated to 18% in 2017 vs. 2016 versus a 10 year CAGR of 9%.
Ecommerce Continues to Grow Ecommerce in the United States continues to grow rapidly. At approximately $450 billion, ecommerce sales grew 16% during 2017 vs. 14% during 2016. Ecommerce represents approximately 13% of total retails sales in the U.S. Again, data collection allows for a more personalized user experience on ecommerce sites. Additionally, ecommerce sites continue to go vertical integrating the purchase, payment, and financing all in one app.
Interestingly, social media often sparks online sales. Online sales typically start at Amazon (49% of users) and search engines (36%). Personalized feeds in applications like Facebook and Instagram often begin the purchase process. The share of social media feed referrals to ecommerce sites was 6% in 2017 vs. 2% in 2015.
Subscribing Versus Purchasing Another trend developing is one to subscribing versus buying. Consumers are no longer buying many products. This is most evident in areas like entertainment with subscription based services such as Netflix and Spotify exhibiting strong growth. Mobile shopping app sessions were up 54% during 2017. Again, social media is helping to spur this activity as many users view videos before making purchases, receive social media referrals, or follow the lead of influencers on social media sites. These trends are hastening the decline of traditional bricks and mortar retail.
Better Prices for Consumers One benefit of the growth in ecommerce has been the decline in prices paid by consumers. Since the beginning of 2016, prices have declined 3% online and 1% offline. Price declines have been steepest in televisions, technology and furniture. Technology has made online shopping more efficient with lower prices, more selection, and increased convenience.
Summary Usage of the internet continues to grow at a healthy pace. New devices and applications have become faster and easier to use. Using data, online sites are able to offer more personalized experiences for users.
* Note that this articles references Internet Trends 2018 published by Mary Meeker at Kleiner Perkins.
